fixture.description: Synthetic 90x120 JPEG (quality=90). Content is a solid-color quadrilateral (120,40,200) on a dark background, physically stored pre-rotated 90deg CCW with EXIF Orientation=6 set, so a spec-correct reader must EXIF-correct it back to the 120x90 upright frame to recover the known ROI at the known corners. Not a real camera photo - see docs/agent-workflow/handoff-T04.md for why.

native_leg.reason: No Android SDK, adb, or physical/emulated device available in this environment (see docs/toolchain-matrix.md, same blocker as T03). modules/capture-native/android/CaptureModule.kt contains real, hand-written source implementing the identical algorithm, but it has never been compiled or executed. Its output is unknown, not assumed to match.

comparison.root_cause_isolated: Verified by direct pixel comparison at raw stored coordinate (45,60), BEFORE any orientation/homography/median code runs: PIL decodes (120,40,201), jpeg-js decodes (119,39,200) at the identical byte-identical JPEG file. The discrepancy is in the two JPEG decoder libraries' internal YCbCr->RGB rounding, not in the shared EXIF-orientation or perspective-homography logic (which agree exactly on orientation tag, output dimensions and sample count).
comparison.conclusion: Shared pipeline logic (EXIF parsing, 8-case orientation correction, Heckbert homography, median aggregation) is verified consistent across JS and Python. Raw JPEG decode is NOT bit-exact across the two decoder libraries used (jpeg-js vs Pillow/libjpeg): a uniform -1 per-channel offset was measured, not assumed. No blanket 'golden vectors agree' claim is made; the measured tolerance is documented here instead.
